options.label: No significant disability despite symptoms; able to carry out all usual duties and activities
Slight disability; unable to carry out all previous activities, but able to look after own affairs without assistance
Moderate disability; requiring some help, but able to walk without assistance
Moderately severe disability; unable to walk without assistance and unable to attend to own bodily needs without assistance
Severe disability; bedridden, incontinent, and requiring constant nursing care and attention

metadata.name: Modified Rankin Scale (mRS)
metadata.summary: 7-grade ordinal measure of global disability and functional independence after stroke.
when_to_use: Quantify pre-stroke baseline disability (for acute reperfusion eligibility) and 90-day post-stroke functional outcome.
next_steps: Document pre-stroke mRS alongside baseline NIHSS when evaluating acute mechanical thrombectomy or IV thrombolysis.
clinical_pearls: Evaluate actual performance and assistance required in daily life, not theoretical capacity.
Pre-stroke mRS is critical when determining acute thrombectomy eligibility.
Standard measure of global functional outcome in stroke clinical trials; correlates with stroke type, infarct size, and other neurological impairment scales.
Pitfall — Subjectivity & interrater variability: Subjective grade boundaries can introduce variability and bias across raters (Banks & Marotta, 2007).
Pitfall — Unstructured interviews: Using a structured interview or simplified questionnaire improves interrater reliability compared with unstructured grading, though some variability remains.

references.citation: van Swieten JC, Koudstaal PJ, Visser MC, Schouten HJ, van Gijn J. Interobserver agreement for the assessment of handicap in stroke patients. Stroke. 1988;19(5):604-607.
Banks JL, Marotta CA. Outcomes validity and reliability of the modified Rankin scale: implications for stroke clinical trials: a literature review and synthesis. Stroke. 2007;38(3):1091-1096.
Fearon P, McArthur KS, Garrity K, et al. Prestroke modified Rankin stroke scale has moderate interobserver reliability and validity in an acute stroke setting. Stroke. 2012;43(12):3184-3188.
López-Cancio E, Salvat M, Cerdà N, et al. Phone and video-based modalities of central blinded adjudication of modified Rankin scores in an endovascular stroke trial. Stroke. 2015;46(12):3405-3410.

interpretation.label: Excellent Functional Outcome
interpretation.summary: mRS 0–1: no symptoms or no significant disability; full return to usual activities.

interpretation.label: Functional Independence (Slight Disability)
interpretation.summary: mRS 2: independent in self-care and household affairs, though some pre-stroke activities are restricted.

interpretation.label: Moderate to Moderately Severe Disability
interpretation.summary: mRS 3–4: requires assistance with instrumental or basic ADLs.

interpretation.label: Severe Disability or Death
interpretation.summary: mRS 5–6: bedridden requiring constant nursing care, or death.

assessment_guides.title: Distinguishing mRS 1 vs mRS 2
bedside_steps: Ask if the patient had to stop work, hobbies, driving, or social activities they previously performed.
pitfalls_and_exceptions: If they can still do ALL usual activities despite mild symptoms -> mRS 1.
If they had to give up any pre-stroke activity (e.g., driving or job) but need zero help from another person -> mRS 2.

assessment_guides.title: Distinguishing mRS 2 vs mRS 3 (Independence Threshold)
bedside_steps: Check whether the patient needs help from another person for shopping, finances, cooking, or housework.
pitfalls_and_exceptions: Using a cane/walker independently WITHOUT human assistance still allows mRS 3 (or 2 if no ADL help needed).
Needing help with instrumental ADLs (bills, cooking, transport) places the patient in mRS 3 even if walking independently.

assessment_guides.title: Distinguishing mRS 3 vs mRS 4
bedside_steps: Assess whether the patient can walk without physical help from another person and manage toileting/dressing.
pitfalls_and_exceptions: If unable to walk without human assistance OR unable to attend to own bodily needs -> mRS 4.
A patient who requires constant 24-hour nursing supervision and is bedridden/incontinent -> mRS 5.
